title: Deterministic bootstrap validation and air-gapped fallback criteria for private/VPC deployments
creator: Ava Reynolds
summary: Define acceptance criteria and clear requirements for a deterministic, verifiable bootstrap process for Private/VPC installations where network egress is restricted or absent. Include fallback behavior when external mirrors or registries are unavailable and define operator actions and automation for staged artifact validation and recovery.
background: Customers operating in regulated environments require Private/VPC deployments that can be bootstrapped and upgraded without outbound egress or with tightly controlled egress windows. Current install flows assume availability of external mirrors or ephemeral egress for image fetch and KMS ops; this ticket clarifies deterministic validation steps, signature and checksum verification, staged artifact sync, and explicit fallback behaviors for air-gapped or restricted networks.
problem_statement: Ambiguity in operator expectations when an offline site cannot reach canonical mirrors during bootstrap or upgrades. Previously documented 'offline upgrade' flows are fragmented across PRDs and runbooks; lack of a deterministic validation protocol leads to manual debugging, inconsistent rollouts, and failed upgrades under strict egress constraints.
goals: Specify a deterministic bootstrap manifest format (seed-manifest) used to validate artifact ordering and dependencies before applying any state changes
Define signature chain and checksum verification requirements that work with customer-managed KMS/HSM and zero-egress validation windows
Specify clear automated fallback behavior and safe operator prompts when staged artifact sync fails or partial artifacts are present
Provide concrete acceptance tests and chaos scenarios that demonstrate safe failure modes and operator recoverability
non_goals: Rewriting existing operator tooling (this ticket defines acceptance criteria and requirements; implementation is tracked in ENG tickets)
Changing encryption algorithms used by customers' KMS/HSM providers
Replacing third-party artifact repositories (we assume customer-configured mirrors will be used where required)
detailed_requirements: Seed-manifest: a single JSON/YAML artifact signed by Redwood and optionally re-signed by customer, containing a deterministic list of images, checksums (sha256), and ordering annotations for initial bootstrap and for any multi-stage upgrades

Manifest verification: runtime must verify signature chain, then validate all listed checksums before pulling or applying artifacts. If any checksum fails, the install must pause and provide a reproducible diagnostic bundle
Delta staging: allow operator to upload a 'staged-mirror' bundle (tarball + manifest) that is applied atomically; installer must validate the bundle locally without requiring outbound egress

Zero-egress validation mode: installer must support a mode that uses only pre-provisioned artifacts and local KMS proxies; any external DNS or API calls in this mode are disallowed and must be explicitly gated behind an operator checkpoint
Graceful partial-sync: if only a subset of artifacts are present, define deterministic 'safe-hold' state where control plane starts in read-only mode until missing critical artifacts are reconciled
Canary policy for multi-site: when syncing a large deployment across sites, support staged application where N% of sites apply changes and health checks run for T minutes before global rollout
Operator prompts & telemetry: installer must emit machine-readable reasons for halts, suggested next steps, and a unique correlation ID that surfaces in monitoring and the diagnostic bundle
KMS integration: support for validating signed manifests using customer KMS (including key rotation checks) with explicit instructions for offline key exchange if necessary
Time-bounded egress windows: when small egress windows are permitted, installer should perform 'fetch, verify, stage, and purge' in a single atomic window and log all network endpoints contacted

Deterministic rollback criteria: define observable signals (e.g., failing health checks, metadata mismatches, state divergence) that trigger automatic rollback to the seed-manifest state within a configured timeout
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: An operator can perform a full bootstrap in zero-egress mode using a staged-mirror bundle; installer verifies signatures and checksums and completes with all services healthy in read-write mode if all artifacts pass

AC-2: If a checksum or signature fails during manifest verification, installer halts before mutating control plane state, emits a diagnostic bundle, and surfaces clear remediation steps to the operator

AC-3: During a simulated network partition where 40% of nodes cannot reach mirrors, deployment enters safe-hold and exposes read-only endpoints; when mirrors become available, staged apply completes without manual state reconciliation

AC-4: Canary rollouts: when configured for 10% canary with 15-minute health window, failing health checks on canaries prevent global rollout and automatically revert canary sites to previous seed-manifest state

AC-5: Time-bounded egress window test: in a 60-second egress window, installer fetches only the artifacts listed in the seed-manifest, validates them locally, and purges transient credentials after completion; all network calls are logged in the runbook

AC-6: KMS validation: manifests signed by Redwood with customer re-signing are validated successfully using customer KMS; rotating the re-signing key causes a clear operator error and documented recovery path
AC-7: Diagnostic correlation: every bootstrap/upgrade run produces a correlation ID that appears in installer logs, Console trace, and the diagnostic bundle saved to the artifacts directory
AC-8: Security review: the design includes a documented threat model covering supply-chain tampering and operators confirm mitigations in a security review
test_plan: TP-1: Zero-egress install with provided staged-mirror bundle (test infra provides signed bundle). Verify installer completes without outbound connections (blocked via network policy) and services become healthy.
TP-2: Corrupt one artifact in the staged bundle and confirm installer halts with checksum error; validate diagnostic bundle contents and suggested remediation.
TP-3: Simulate partial mirror availability across zones and assert safe-hold behavior; then restore mirrors and assert automatic completion within configured timeout.
TP-4: Canary failure injection: degrade one canary site (simulate pod crash loop) and confirm rollout aborts and canary sites roll back automatically.
TP-5: Egress-window timing: schedule a 30s, 60s, and 120s egress window; measure success rate and log all endpoints contacted; establish recommended minimum window for typical cluster sizes.
TP-6: KMS rotation test: rotate customer signing key in test KMS and verify recovery instructions produce successful re-signing path
rollout_plan: 1) Design review with Security & Infra teams and sign-off on manifest format
2) Implement manifest parser and verification in installer (ENG ticket references will be added)
3) Provide sample staged-mirror bundles and automated test harness for customers
4) Pilot with two existing large-regulated customers in a controlled maintenance window
5) General availability release with runbook updates and Console UI additions to surface correlation IDs and staged apply state
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: manifest-verification-failure-high (threshold: >5 failures in 10m for same customer)
Tracing: include correlation_id across installer, operator-actions, and console logs
security_considerations: Threat: supply-chain tampering of artifacts. Mitigation: signature chain verification, reproducible checksums, optional customer re-signing
Threat: leakage during egress windows. Mitigation: ephemeral credentials, single-window fetch-and-purge, outbound audit logs
Threat: malicious staged bundle. Mitigation: require bundle signing and enforce signature validation and integrity checks before any state mutation
